LanguageData.ContentedLivestock.Settings.Scope: Settings are global and saved when you close this window. Changes apply when play resumes; contentment then changes gradually. Closing also refreshes animal eligibility and pasture/company observations. RIMMSQOL and compatible tools can reveal an optional main-button shortcut to this same page; it is hidden by default.
LanguageData.ContentedLivestock.Tip.Rate: Filling with milk, wool or eggs at {0} of the usual rate.
LanguageData.ContentedLivestock.Tip.Halted: Too miserable to produce. Production freezes until conditions improve.
LanguageData.ContentedLivestock.Settings.Intro: Colony animals keep a contentment need built from how they are kept. Contentment sets how fast they fill with milk, wool and eggs — and below a floor, whether they fill at all.
LanguageData.ContentedLivestock.Settings.FloorTip: An animal below this level stops filling entirely. It keeps whatever it had already accumulated. Set to 0% to never stop production.
LanguageData.ContentedLivestock.Settings.PlateauTip: At this level the animal fills at exactly the vanilla rate. Below it the rate ramps down to the floor; above it, up to the maximum.
LanguageData.ContentedLivestock.Settings.MinRateTip: The rate just above the floor, as a share of the vanilla rate.
LanguageData.ContentedLivestock.Settings.MaxRateTip: The rate at full contentment. Set to 100% for a mod that only ever penalises.
LanguageData.ContentedLivestock.Settings.SpeedTip: How far contentment can travel in a day. At 100% an animal takes a full day to go from miserable to content, or the reverse.
LanguageData.ContentedLivestock.Settings.FeedTip: Grazing living plants is best, then raw produce and meat, then hay, then kibble. The memory of the last meal fades over two days.
LanguageData.ContentedLivestock.Settings.SpaceTip: Roped animals are judged on whether their pen grows back faster than the herd eats it — the figure the pen marker already shows. Everything else is judged on floor space per animal in its room.
LanguageData.ContentedLivestock.Settings.TemperatureT: Measured against each animal's own comfortable range, so a heated barn matters to a chicken and not to a husky.
LanguageData.ContentedLivestock.Settings.HealthTip: Pain, bleeding and hunger all pull contentment down.
LanguageData.ContentedLivestock.Settings.CompanyTip: A bond with a colonist helps. A herd animal kept away from its own kind suffers.
LanguageData.ContentedLivestock.Settings.ProducersOnl: Only animals that give milk, wool or eggs have contentment
On, only animals that give milk, wool or eggs keep a contentment need. Off, every colony animal does — including pets and pack animals, for whom it shows but changes nothing.
